title: Which devices are failing posture: the Failed Posture Devices page and the dashboard's Device Posture page

prose.text: {{availability}} Telemetry is in [[zcc.support-options]]; why a check fails is in [[zcc.device-posture.failure-modes]].

prose.label: Dashboard Device Posture page.
prose.text: {{dashboard-filters}} {{dashboard-widgets}} The other dashboard pages are in [[zcc.devices.dashboard]].

prose.label: Open questions.
prose.text: The 7-day and 14-day reach, platforms beyond Windows and macOS, and how Count relates to evaluation are open {{gap:coverage-details}}.

checks.do: For a page that lists no failed devices, whether Digital Experience (ZDX) or Client Connector Telemetry is enabled.

availability.statement: The Failed Posture Devices page and the dashboard's Device Posture page are available only if Digital Experience (ZDX) or Client Connector Telemetry is enabled.

quotes: Failed Posture Devices is available only if you have Digital Experience (ZDX) or Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry enabled.
The Device Posture page is available only if you have Digital Experience (ZDX) or Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry enabled.

page-filters.statement: The Failed Posture Devices page (Infrastructure > Client Connector > Failed Posture Devices) lists devices that failed posture checks, filtered by Time (three-hour intervals up to 24 hours), Failed Device Posture (one posture profile) and OS (Windows, macOS or both; both shown by default).

quotes: From the Zscaler Admin Console, you can view a list of devices that failed posture checks.
On the Failed Posture Devices page (Infrastructure > Client Connector > Failed Posture Devices), you can do the following:
Time: View devices for failed postures ranging from three-hour intervals up to 24 hours.
Failed Device Posture: View failed devices for that specific device posture profile.
OS: View devices for either Windows or macOS or for both of the operating systems. By default, both operating systems are shown.

export.statement: The list exports as a CSV file: Export All exports all devices for a chosen time interval of up to 24 hours within the past 14 days, and Export View exports the information currently visible on the page.

quotes: Export the list of devices as a CSV file.

Select Export All to export the information for all devices and then select a time interval to export the information for a specific time frame up to 24 hours within the past 14 days. Select Export View to export the information currently visible on the page.

columns.statement: For each device the list shows User ID, OS Type, Device Model, First Failure Time, Last Failure Time and Count (the number of times the device posture failed for the device), and each page shows up to 50 devices by default.

quotes: User ID: The enrolled user for the device.
OS Type: The device operating system.
Device Model: The device model.
First Failure Time: The time and date the first posture failure occurred.
Last Failure Time: The time and date the most recent posture failure occurred.
Count: The number of times the device posture failed for the device.
By default, each page shows up to 50 devices.

dashboard-filters.statement: The dashboard's Device Posture page filters by Time (failed-posture times in three-hour intervals up to 24 hours, with data shown up to the past 7 days) and OS (Windows, macOS or both; both shown by default).

quotes: Time: Modify the failed postures times ranging from three-hour intervals up to 24 hours. You can set the filter to show data up to the past 7 days.
OS: View devices for either Windows or macOS or for both of the operating systems. By default, both operating systems are shown.

dashboard-widgets.statement: The Device Posture page's widgets are Top 10 Failed Device Posture Trend, Top 50 Failed Posture Profiles, Top 10 Non-Compliant Devices and Compliant vs Non-Compliant. The widget descriptions cover the trendline of the top 10 posture profiles with the most failing devices (or of up to 10 profiles chosen in the Top 50 Failed Posture Profiles widget), the top 50 profiles by failing devices (a click opens the failed devices on the Failed Devices page), the number of non-compliant devices for the top 10 failures by profile, and compliant against non-compliant devices for the top 10 failed profiles with each profile's failure total and trend.

quotes: - Top 10 Failed Device Posture Trend
- Top 50 Failed Posture Profiles
- Top 10 Non-Compliant Devices
- Compliant vs Non-Compliant
This widget displays the trendline of the top 10 device posture profiles that have the highest number of devices failing their device posture checks.
You can select a different set of up to 10 device posture profiles in the Top 50 Failed Posture Profiles widget to view the trendline for those profiles.
This widget displays the top 50 device posture profiles that have the highest number of devices failing their posture checks.
You can click a device posture profile to view the failed devices on the Failed Devices page.
This widget displays the total number of non-compliant devices for the top 10 device posture failures and the distribution of the devices by device posture profile.
This widget displays the number of devices with the top 10 failed device posture profiles that are compliant (passed the posture check) and non-compliant (failed the posture check).
For the non-compliant devices, the widget displays the total number of posture failures and the upwards or downwards trend for each device posture profile.

coverage-details.title: Reach, platforms and Count on the failed-posture pages
coverage-details.detail: The dashboard page shows data up to the past 7 days while the list exports reach back 14 days, and the pages do not say why. Both OS filters offer Windows and macOS only, so whether Linux or mobile failures appear is not stated, and how Count relates to the posture evaluation cadence (zpa.posture-profiles.evaluation:cadence) is not described.
